ministry: Ministry of Women and Child Development
title: Ministry introduced Anganwadi cum Creches under Palna for providing day care creche facilities in safe and secure environment to children
text:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau

Ministry of Women and Child Development

Ministry introduced Anganwadi cum Creches under Palna for providing day care creche facilities in safe and secure environment to children

प्रविष्टि तिथि:
12 AUG 2026 4:03PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry introduced Anganwadi cum Creches (AWCCs) under Palna Scheme w.e.f. 01 April 2022, for providing day care creche facilities in safe and secure environment to children (aged 06 months – 06 years) of all mothers irrespective of their employment status along with nutritional support, health and cognitive development of children, growth monitoring, immunization, education etc. Palna component under Samarthya vertical of Mission Shakti is a centrally sponsored scheme and is implemented with a funding ratio of 60:40 between Centre and State Governments and UTs with legislature except North East & Special Category States where ratio is 90:10. For UTs without legislature, 100% funding is provided by the Central Government.
 Funds under the Scheme are released to the States/UTs in accordance with the guidelines of the Department of Expenditure through the
Single Nodal Agency (SNA)/SNA-SPARSH
 mechanism of the Public Financial Management System (PFMS). Presently, a total of 4,172 Anganwadi-cum-Crèches (AWCCs) are operational across the country.

Ministry of Labour and Employment has informed that the provisions of the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 have been subsumed under the Code on Social Security, 2020, which came into effect on 21.11.2025. Section 67 of the Code on Social Security, 2020 provides for creche facilities for establishment with 50 or more employees. Under the Code, enforcement in respect of establishments under the State Sphere is the responsibility of the respective State Governments. Chief Labour Commissioner (Central) Organisation under the Ministry of Labour and Employment is the designated enforcement authority for ensuring compliance with maternity benefit provisions in establishments under the Central Sphere.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Women and Child Development Smt. Savitri Thakur in Rajya Sabha in reply to a question.
